subject.title: feat(clients): provider-grouped model picker with fast, verbosity, and inherited-thinking controls

question: Should native Fast mode reuse the existing web provider-support boundary now, or should OpenClaw first introduce a gateway-delivered provider capability contract for all clients?
rationale: `models.list` does not currently expose a Fast-capability field, while the web client already has a narrower provider mapping; choosing a permanent cross-client capability source is a maintainer-facing product and API direction decision.

options.title: Reuse the existing web capability boundary
options.body: Gate native Fast mode with the existing supported-provider behavior and keep the change scoped to parity until a shared capability contract is designed.

options.title: Design a gateway capability contract first
options.body: Add an explicit provider/model Fast capability to the gateway payload, then have web and native clients consume that single contract.

options.title: Defer Fast mode from this parity round
options.body: Land only the provider grouping, verbosity, and thinking work after their correctness fixes, leaving Fast for a separately scoped capability change.

recommendation.title: Reuse the existing web capability boundary
recommendation.body: Gate native Fast mode with the existing supported-provider behavior and keep the change scoped to parity until a shared capability contract is designed.

likelyOwner.reason: This contributor owns the immediately adjacent native-chat parity implementation and can route the cross-client decision with the relevant feature context.
